title: The new edge in agent tooling is control inside the runtime
summary: Three releases in three days moved on the same axis: event surfaces, sandbox escalation, authorization and scheduling. Capability is no longer the differentiator; what happens while an agent is running is.
thesis: The strongest releases this week hardened the mechanics that keep an agent useful after the demo, not the mechanics that make the demo work.

items.name: Pydantic AI Harness
items.platform: Python 3.10+; the project does not state an OS matrix
items.what: FileSystem traversal events now reach RepoContext through @on_event, and a repo-defined Pydantic AI agent can run inside GitHub Agentic Workflows.
items.whyDifferent: Evented plumbing plus a route to run the agent inside GitHub Actions, rather than another capability bolted onto the harness.

items.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
items.platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; PowerShell v6+ on Windows
items.what: Windows sandbox runs can record blocked access and take a constrained escalation before any full bypass, and Vim mode is now generally available. This is a pre-release.
items.whyDifferent: Sandbox policy is enforced inside the coding-agent loop rather than around it, so a blocked call becomes an observable event instead of a failure.

items.name: Hermes Agent
items.platform: Native Windows 10/11 supported but documented as early beta; WSL2, Linux and macOS are more established
items.what: The patch rolls up desktop session controls, MCP authorization, cron scheduling and delivery fixes, and delegation reliability work.
items.whyDifferent: A broad always-on runtime with session, authorization and scheduling in one place, rather than a narrow coding harness.

items.name: Mastra Factory Beta
items.what: An open-source software factory that connects GitHub, Linear and Slack, moving issue intake, planning, implementation and PR review through configurable agent stages.
items.whyDifferent: Mastra publishes its own alpha counts rather than only a headline range: 277 of 1,627 merged PRs authored (17.0%) and 222 of 778 issues closed (28.5%). The same post also claims 25-35% of PRs and 50-60% of issues; where a claim and its underlying table disagree, the table is the figure worth carrying.

readThrough: Teams evaluating agents should now inspect event surfaces, sandbox policy, authorization, scheduling and recovery — not just model quality or tool count. The question has moved from what an agent can do to whether it stays governed while doing it.
